examples.en: The match is being broadcast on TV.
They streamed the concert online yesterday.
They will broadcast the final tomorrow evening.

examples.ko: 현장에서 뉴스를 중계하는 기자가 많이 바빠 보여요.
examples.en: The reporter covering the news live at the scene looks very busy.

examples.ko: 공연을 중계하고 나서 시청자들이 댓글을 많이 달았어요.
examples.en: After they broadcast the show, viewers left lots of comments.
The baseball game was being broadcast on the radio, so I listened while driving.

explain: 스포츠나 공연을 현장에서 다른 곳으로 바로 전해 보여 줄 때 써요. 녹화한 것을 나중에 틀면 보통 '재방송'이라고 하고, 지금 일어나는 일임을 강조할 때는 '생중계'라고 해요. '경기를 중계하다', '방송을 중계하다'처럼 목적어와 함께 써요.
explain_en: Used when a sports match or a show is sent live from the scene to viewers elsewhere. A recording shown later is usually called '재방송' (rerun), and '생중계' stresses that it is happening right now. It takes an object: '경기를 중계하다', '방송을 중계하다'.

examples.en: A white crane is standing by the lake.

examples.ko: 학은 오래 사는 동물로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: The crane is known as a long-living animal.
I saw a crane for the first time at the zoo.

examples.ko: 그림 속에 학 두 마리가 날고 있어요.
examples.en: Two cranes are flying in the painting.

examples.ko: 한국 옛 그림에는 소나무와 학이 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Pine trees and cranes often appear in old Korean paintings.

examples.ko: 학처럼 다리가 긴 새는 물가에서 살아요.
examples.en: Birds with long legs like cranes live near the water.

explain: 한국 옛 그림에서 학은 오래 사는 동물이라 건강과 오래 사는 삶을 빌 때 소나무와 함께 그려요. 같은 새를 순우리말로는 '두루미'라고 하는데, 일상에서는 '학'과 '두루미'를 둘 다 써요. '학교'의 '학'과는 소리만 같고 전혀 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: In old Korean paintings the crane stands for a long, healthy life, so it is often drawn with pine trees. The native Korean word for the same bird is '두루미', and both words are used. It sounds the same as the '학' in '학교' (school), but they are unrelated.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 옛 모습 그대로 보존돼요.
examples.en: This building is preserved just as it used to look.
The dinosaur bones were well preserved underground.

examples.ko: 냉동실에 넣으면 음식이 더 오래 보존될 거예요.
examples.en: Food will keep longer if you put it in the freezer.

examples.ko: 잘 보존되는 문화재는 관리하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Well-preserved cultural properties have many people looking after them.

examples.ko: 자연이 보존되고 나서 새들이 다시 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: After nature was preserved, the birds came back.

examples.ko: 사진이 잘 보존돼서 백 년 전 모습을 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: The photos are well preserved, so we can see how it looked a hundred years ago.

explain: '보관되다'는 어디에 두었는지가 중요하고, '보존되다'는 원래 상태가 변하지 않았다는 점이 중요해요. 문화재, 자연, 식품, 자료에 많이 써요. 사람이 하면 '보존하다', 그 결과로 남아 있으면 '보존되다'예요.
explain_en: '보관되다' focuses on where something is kept, while '보존되다' focuses on the original condition not changing. It is common with cultural assets, nature, food and records. A person does '보존하다'; the result is '보존되다'.

examples.en: The museum preserves old bowls.

examples.ko: 우리는 숲을 보존하려고 쓰레기를 줍고 있어요.
examples.en: We are picking up trash to preserve the forest.

examples.ko: 할머니가 오래된 한복을 상자에 넣어 잘 보존하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother put the old hanbok in a box and preserved it well.

examples.ko: 음식을 오래 보존할 수 있는 방법이 있어요?
examples.en: Is there a way to keep food for a long time?
Preserving nature is important to everyone.

examples.ko: 사진을 잘 보존해서 아이들에게 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: I kept the photos in good condition and showed them to the kids.

explain: '보관하다'는 물건을 어디에 두는 일이고, '보존하다'는 상태가 변하지 않게 지키는 일이에요. 자연, 문화재, 전통, 자료에 자주 써요. '자연 보존'처럼 명사로도 많이 쓰고, 일상에서 물건을 챙길 때는 '보관하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '보관하다' is about putting something somewhere; '보존하다' is about protecting it so its condition does not change. Common with nature, heritage, tradition and records. For everyday belongings, '보관하다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: He admitted his mistake right away.
The company admitted its mistake and apologized.
We were surprised because my friend admitted the lie.
It is not easy to admit your mistakes.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 규칙을 어긴 것을 시인할 거예요.
examples.en: The player will admit that he broke the rules.
He never admitted it, so the problem dragged on.

explain: 숨기고 싶은 잘못이나 사실을 인정할 때 써요. 뉴스와 공식적인 자리에서 자주 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '인정하다'가 더 흔해요. 같은 소리의 '시인'은 시를 쓰는 사람(poet)이라서 문장 속 위치로 구분해요.
explain_en: Used when someone admits a fault or a fact they wanted to hide. It shows up in news and formal settings; in daily talk '인정하다' is more common. The word '시인' with the same sound also means a poet, so read it by context.

examples.en: The air conditioner temperature is adjusted automatically.
The volume was adjusted with a button.
Prices will be controlled by government policy.
It is a self-adjusting chair, so it is comfortable.
My blood pressure is well controlled with medicine.
The light is adjusted, so my eyes are less tired.

explain: 온도, 소리, 속도, 양을 알맞은 정도로 맞출 때 써요. '조정하다'는 시간이나 기준을 바꾸는 일이고, '조종하다'는 비행기나 기계를 직접 움직이는 일이라서 서로 달라요. 사람이 하면 '조절하다', 저절로 맞춰지면 '조절되다'예요.
explain_en: Used when temperature, sound, speed or amount is set to a suitable level. '조정하다' changes a schedule or standard, and '조종하다' means operating a plane or machine, so they differ. A person does '조절하다'; when it adjusts by itself it is '조절되다'.

examples.en: That old rule is being abolished this year.
The show was cancelled because it was not popular.

examples.ko: 이 버스 노선은 다음 달에 폐지될 거예요.
examples.en: This bus route will be discontinued next month.

examples.ko: 폐지되는 제도가 많아서 안내문이 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Many systems are being abolished, so notices come out often.

examples.ko: 법이 폐지되고 나서 사람들의 생활이 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: After the law was repealed, people's lives changed.
The exam system was abolished, and the students were happy.

explain: 법, 제도, 서비스, 프로그램이 더 이상 없어질 때 써요. 가게나 회사가 문을 닫는 일은 '폐업하다', '문을 닫다'라고 해요. 사람이 없애면 '폐지하다', 없어지는 쪽이 주어면 '폐지되다'예요.
explain_en: Used when a law, system, service or program ceases to exist. A shop or company closing is '폐업하다' or '문을 닫다' instead. The one who ends it does '폐지하다'; the thing that ends is '폐지되다'.

examples.en: The road is closed off because of an accident.
Spam texts were blocked automatically.

examples.ko: 그 사이트는 우리 학교에서 차단될 거예요.
examples.en: That site will be blocked at our school.

examples.ko: 차단되는 번호는 전화가 와도 울리지 않아요.
examples.en: A blocked number does not ring even when it calls.
The sunlight is blocked, so the room is cool.

examples.ko: 한 번 차단되고 나면 메시지를 보낼 수 없어요.
examples.en: Once you are blocked, you cannot send messages.

explain: '막히다'는 길이나 코처럼 자연스럽게 막힌 상태에도 쓰지만, '차단되다'는 누군가 일부러 못 지나가게 한 경우에 써요. 번호, 사이트, 햇빛, 소음에 자주 써요. 사람이 하면 '차단하다', 막힌 쪽은 '차단되다'예요.
explain_en: '막히다' can describe a naturally blocked road or nose, but '차단되다' is for something deliberately kept from passing. It is common with phone numbers, websites, sunlight and noise. The one who blocks does '차단하다'; the blocked side is '차단되다'.

examples.en: I reside in Seoul.
My foreign friend lived in Busan for five years.
Next year I will live in the countryside.

examples.ko: 이 건물에 거주하는 사람은 모두 학생이에요.
examples.en: Everyone living in this building is a student.

examples.ko: 한국에 거주하고 있어서 한국 음식이 익숙해요.
examples.en: I live in Korea, so Korean food is familiar to me.
I live near the office, so commuting is easy.

explain: '살다'와 같은 일을 가리키지만 서류, 뉴스, 공식적인 자리에서 써요. 친구와 이야기할 때는 '서울에 살아요'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '거주지', '거주자', '거주 기간'처럼 명사로도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It describes the same thing as '살다' but fits forms, news and formal situations. With friends, '서울에 살아요' sounds much more natural. It also appears in nouns such as '거주지' (residence) and '거주자' (resident).

en: be identified; be understood; be figured out

examples.en: The cause of the accident has not been identified yet.
What customers want can be grasped through a survey.

examples.ko: 문제가 빨리 파악돼서 바로 고칠 수 있었어요.
examples.en: The problem was found quickly, so we could fix it right away.

examples.ko: 파악되는 정보가 적어서 더 조사해야 해요.
examples.en: Little information has been confirmed, so we need to investigate more.
The scale of the damage will be determined tomorrow.
We started the meeting after the situation was understood.

explain: '알다'보다 상황이나 원인을 정확하게 확인해서 이해했다는 느낌이 강해요. 뉴스에서는 '아직 파악되지 않았다'처럼 부정형으로 가장 많이 나와요. 사람이 하면 '파악하다', 조사로 알게 되면 '파악되다'예요.
explain_en: Stronger than '알다': it suggests you checked and clearly understood a situation or cause. In the news it appears most often in the negative, '아직 파악되지 않았다' (not yet identified). A person does '파악하다'; what becomes known through investigation is '파악되다'.

examples.en: The company sponsors the marathon.
I supported a children's organization every month.

examples.ko: 팬들이 가수의 새 앨범을 후원할 거예요.
examples.en: Fans will back the singer's new album.

examples.ko: 후원하는 사람이 많아서 행사가 잘 끝났어요.
examples.en: Many people sponsored it, so the event ended well.

examples.ko: 동네 가게가 학교 축제를 후원하고 있어요.
examples.en: A neighborhood shop is sponsoring the school festival.
They supported poor students and set up a scholarship.

explain: 돈이나 물건으로 어떤 사람, 단체, 행사를 도울 때 써요. '도와주다'보다 공식적이고 꾸준히 돕는 느낌이 있어요. '후원금', '후원자', '후원 계좌'처럼 함께 나오는 말이 많아요.
explain_en: Used when you help a person, group or event with money or goods. It sounds more formal and ongoing than '도와주다'. It pairs with '후원금' (donation), '후원자' (supporter) and '후원 계좌' (donation account).

examples.en: A camera is fitted on new cars.
This phone is equipped with a big battery.

examples.ko: 내년에는 안전 장치가 모두 장착될 거예요.
examples.en: Next year all the safety devices will be installed.
The fitted parts are different, so the prices differ too.

examples.ko: 렌즈가 장착되고 나서 사진이 더 선명해졌어요.
examples.en: After the lens was attached, the photos got sharper.
Airbags are installed, so it is safer.

explain: 제품 소개나 뉴스에서 자주 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '달려 있다', '들어 있다'를 더 많이 써요. 사람이 달면 '장착하다', 달려 있는 상태가 되면 '장착되다'예요. '카메라가 장착된 차'처럼 뒤 명사를 꾸며 주는 모양으로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It appears often in product descriptions and the news; in everyday talk Koreans say '달려 있다' or '들어 있다' more often. The person who installs it uses '장착하다'; the part that ends up installed is '장착되다'. It is also common as a modifier, as in '카메라가 장착된 차' (a car fitted with a camera).

examples.en: The landlord rents the room out to a student.
The company leased the office for three years.
I will lease out the shop from next year.
A house for rent needs a deposit.
I rent out a building and collect monthly rent.

examples.ko: 공원 앞에서 자전거를 임대해 주는 가게가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a shop in front of the park that rents out bicycles.

explain: 주로 빌려주는 쪽이 하는 일이에요. 빌리는 사람은 '빌리다'나 '세 들다'를 써요. 집이나 사무실 광고에 '임대'가 자주 보여요. 매달 내는 돈은 '월세', 큰 보증금을 맡겼다가 나갈 때 돌려받는 한국식 계약은 '전세'예요.
explain_en: Mostly the lender's action. The person who borrows says '빌리다' or '세 들다'. You often see '임대' on ads for houses and offices. '월세' is rent paid every month; '전세' is the Korean lease where you leave a large deposit and get it back when you move out.

examples.en: According to the test, it is diagnosed as a cold.
The child was diagnosed with the flu.

examples.ko: 병원에서 다시 검사하면 정확하게 진단될 거예요.
examples.en: If you get tested again at the hospital, it will be diagnosed accurately.
It took two days to get a diagnosis.
The problem was diagnosed early, so treatment was easy.

examples.ko: 기계 고장도 컴퓨터로 진단될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Machine faults can also be diagnosed by computer.

explain: '독감으로 진단되다'처럼 '으로/로'와 함께 써요. 환자가 말할 때는 '진단을 받다'가 더 자연스러워서 '병원에서 독감 진단을 받았어요'라고 해요. 기계나 회사 상태를 살필 때도 써요.
explain_en: Used with '(으)로' as in '독감으로 진단되다' (be diagnosed with the flu). When a patient talks about it, '진단을 받다' sounds more natural: '병원에서 독감 진단을 받았어요'. It can also be used for machines or a company's condition.

examples.en: A caterpillar transforms into a butterfly.
The actor transformed into a villain in the movie.
On the weekend I will turn into a chef at home.
I bought a transforming robot toy.
I got a haircut and look completely different.
I was surprised that the plain bag turned into a party bag.

explain: '변하다'는 어떤 변화든 쓰지만 '변신하다'는 겉모습이나 역할이 확 달라질 때만 써요. 만화나 영화 이야기에 많이 나오고, 외모가 확 바뀐 친구에게 '완전 변신했네요!'라고 칭찬할 때도 써요.
explain_en: '변하다' covers any change, but '변신하다' is for a big shift in appearance or role. It is common in cartoons and movies, and you can praise a friend's new look with '완전 변신했네요!'.

examples.en: A new plan is being discussed at the meeting.
That issue was discussed for a long time yesterday.
The budget will be discussed next week.

examples.ko: 논의되는 내용은 모두 메일로 알려 줄게요.
examples.en: I will send you everything that is discussed by email.
We decided after the opinions were fully discussed.
Several methods were discussed, so it is hard to choose.

explain: 안건이나 문제가 주어이고, 회의나 공식적인 자리에서 이야기가 오갈 때 써요. 친구끼리 편하게 이야기하는 일에는 잘 쓰지 않고, 그때는 '이야기하다'를 써요. 사람이 하면 '논의하다'예요.
explain_en: The subject is an agenda item or issue that is being talked over in a meeting or formal setting. For casual chats between friends use '이야기하다' instead. When a person does it, it is '논의하다'.

examples.en: This app works even on old phones.
The machine suddenly does not work.
The new program ran well.
It will start working as soon as you turn the power on.
I am looking for a computer that works normally.

examples.ko: 한글 입력이 동작해서 편하게 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: Korean input works, so I can type comfortably.

explain: 기계나 프로그램이 제대로 돌아갈 때 주로 써요. 일상에서는 '작동하다'나 '되다'라고 더 자주 말해요: '이 앱이 안 돼요'. 사람 몸의 움직임은 '움직이다'를 쓰고, 명사 '동작'은 몸짓이나 자세를 가리켜요.
explain_en: Mostly used when a machine or program runs properly. In daily speech people more often say '작동하다' or '되다', as in '이 앱이 안 돼요'. For human body movement use '움직이다'; the noun '동작' means a gesture or motion.

examples.en: Accidents are prevented by the new system.
Locking the door prevents theft.

examples.ko: 손을 자주 씻으면 감염이 방지될 거예요.
examples.en: Infection will be prevented if you wash your hands often.

examples.ko: 이 장치 덕분에 방지되는 사고가 많아요.
examples.en: Thanks to this device, many accidents are prevented.
After the fire was averted, the residents felt relieved.
Noise is blocked, so it is quiet even at night.

explain: 병이나 건강은 '예방', 사고·범죄·재발은 '방지'를 주로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '막다'를 더 많이 쓰고, 안내문이나 뉴스에서 '재발 방지', '사고 방지'로 자주 봐요. 사람이 하면 '방지하다', 막힌 결과를 말하면 '방지되다'예요.
explain_en: For illness and health Koreans use '예방'; for accidents, crime and recurrence they mostly use '방지'. In everyday talk '막다' is more common, while notices and the news often have '재발 방지' and '사고 방지'. The person acting says '방지하다'; the result that gets prevented is '방지되다'.

examples.ko: 내일은 전국에 비가 올 것으로 예측돼요.
examples.en: Rain is predicted across the country tomorrow.
It was predicted that there would be many travelers this year.

examples.ko: 다음 주부터 기온이 크게 떨어질 것으로 예측되고 있어요.
examples.en: Temperatures are predicted to drop sharply from next week.

examples.ko: 예측되는 결과와 실제 결과가 많이 달랐어요.
examples.en: The predicted result and the actual result were very different.
After the problem was foreseen, we prepared ahead of time.
The result was easy to predict, so it was not fun.

explain: '~(으)ㄹ 것으로 예측되다'라는 형태로 가장 많이 써요. '예측'은 자료와 근거로 미리 말하는 것이고, '예상'은 그냥 그럴 거라고 생각하는 거예요. 일기예보와 뉴스에서 자주 들어요.
explain_en: Most often used in the pattern '~(으)ㄹ 것으로 예측되다'. '예측' is based on data and evidence, while '예상' is simply what you expect. You hear it a lot in weather forecasts and news.

examples.en: When you type a number, it is entered automatically.
My name was entered incorrectly.

examples.ko: 데이터가 모두 입력될 때까지 기다려 주세요.
examples.en: Please wait until all the data is entered.
The characters being entered show on the screen right away.
After the address was entered, the map appeared.
It was entered wrong, so I have to write it again.

explain: 컴퓨터나 폰에 글자, 숫자, 정보가 들어갈 때 써요. 사람이 치면 '입력하다', 저장된 결과를 말하면 '입력되다'예요. 반대말은 '출력되다'이고, 앱 화면에서는 '입력해 주세요'라는 안내를 자주 봐요.
explain_en: Used when letters, numbers or information go into a computer or phone. A person types it with '입력하다'; the stored result is '입력되다'. The opposite is '출력되다' (be output), and apps often show '입력해 주세요' (please enter).

examples.en: I get addicted to games.
He became addicted to coffee.

examples.ko: 상한 음식을 먹으면 중독될 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can get food poisoning if you eat spoiled food.

examples.ko: 스마트폰에 중독되는 사람이 점점 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More and more people are getting hooked on smartphones.
After being poisoned by gas, I went to the hospital.
I am hooked on sweet snacks and it is hard to quit.

explain: '게임에 중독되다'처럼 'N에 중독되다' 형태로 써요. 습관을 끊기 어렵다는 뜻과 몸에 독이 들어갔다는 뜻이 있는데, 독 쪽은 '식중독', '가스 중독'처럼 이어 나와요. 가볍게 '이 노래에 중독됐어요'라고 하면 계속 듣고 싶다는 표현이에요.
explain_en: Used in the pattern 'N에 중독되다'. It covers both a habit that is hard to quit and poison entering the body; the poison sense appears in compounds like '식중독' (food poisoning) and '가스 중독'. Lightly, '이 노래에 중독됐어요' means you cannot stop listening to the song.

examples.ko: 트럭에 짐 탑재 작업이 오래 걸려서 힘들어요.
examples.en: Loading cargo onto the truck takes a long time and is hard work.

examples.ko: 이 폰은 새 칩 탑재로 속도가 빨라졌어요.
examples.en: This phone got faster thanks to the new chip it carries.

examples.ko: 탑재 용량이 큰 배라서 짐을 많이 실을 수 있어요.
examples.en: It is a ship with a large capacity, so it can carry lots of cargo.

examples.ko: 이 안경은 카메라 탑재가 가장 큰 특징이에요.
examples.en: The biggest feature of these glasses is the built-in camera.
A robot with built-in AI talks with people.

examples.ko: 비행기에 짐 탑재를 마친 뒤 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: After finishing loading the luggage onto the plane, they closed the door.

explain: 'AI 탑재', '카메라 탑재'처럼 제품 소개나 광고에 아주 많이 나와요. 원래는 배나 비행기에 짐을 싣는 일을 가리켰어요. 일상 대화에서는 '들어 있다', '달려 있다'가 더 흔하고, 뒤에 '하다'나 '되다'를 붙여 동사로도 써요.
explain_en: Very common in product descriptions and ads, as in 'AI 탑재' or '카메라 탑재' (equipped with AI/a camera). It originally meant loading cargo onto a ship or plane. In daily speech people say '들어 있다' or '달려 있다', and '하다' or '되다' can be added to make a verb.

examples.en: The factory processes meat.

examples.ko: 사진을 가공해서 색을 더 밝게 만들었어요.
examples.en: I edited the photo to make the colors brighter.

examples.ko: 우리는 우유를 가공해 치즈를 만들 거예요.
examples.en: We will process milk to make cheese.
Nutrients decrease during processing.
Processed food is easy to store.
After processing the raw materials, we put them in boxes.

explain: 원재료나 자료를 손질해서 다른 상태로 만들 때 써요. '가공식품'은 이미 손질해서 파는 음식이고, 사진을 보정할 때도 '가공했다'고 해요. '가공의 인물'에서 쓰는 '가공'은 지어낸 이야기라는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: Used when raw materials or data are worked into another form. '가공식품' is processed food, and editing a photo can also be '가공하다'. The '가공' in '가공의 인물' (a fictional person) is a different word meaning made up.

en: reach; get to (a goal or level)

examples.en: The plane reaches its destination.
Our team finally reached the final.
Prices will reach their highest level.

examples.ko: 정상에 도달하는 데 세 시간이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took three hours to reach the summit.

examples.ko: 소리가 먼 곳까지 도달해서 모두 들었어요.
examples.en: The sound reached far away, so everyone heard it.
After reaching my goal, I celebrated with friends.

explain: '도착하다'는 장소에 닿을 때 쓰고, '도달하다'는 목표, 수준, 한계처럼 힘들게 다다르는 곳에 써요. '공항에 도착하다'라고 하지 '공항에 도달하다'라고는 잘 안 해요. '~에 도달하다'처럼 '에'와 함께 써요.
explain_en: '도착하다' is for arriving at a place, while '도달하다' is for reaching a goal, level or limit, often after effort. You say '공항에 도착하다', not '공항에 도달하다'. It takes '에': '~에 도달하다'.

examples.en: A big company takes over a small one.
My older brother took over the shop.
I will take delivery of my new car tomorrow.
The takeover price is so high that I am worried.

examples.ko: 업무를 인수하고 나서 매일 늦게까지 일했어요.
examples.en: After taking over the work, I worked late every day.

examples.ko: 물건을 인수한 뒤 문제가 있으면 말해 주세요.
examples.en: After you receive the item, please tell me if there is a problem.

explain: 회사나 가게를 사서 이어받거나, 물건과 업무를 넘겨받을 때 써요. 반대말은 넘겨주는 '인계하다'이고, 일을 넘기고 받는 과정을 '인수인계'라고 한 세트로 말해요. 신문에서는 회사 이야기에 가장 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Used for buying and taking over a company or shop, or for receiving goods and duties. The opposite is '인계하다' (hand over), and the whole handover process is called '인수인계'. In newspapers it most often appears in company news.

examples.en: City Hall organizes this festival.
The student council ran the sports day.
The teacher will be in charge of the next event.
The person in charge of the event gives a greeting.
I ran the contest, so there was a lot to prepare.

examples.ko: 주관한 회사 이름이 포스터에 나와 있어요.
examples.en: The name of the company that ran it is on the poster.

explain: 행사를 실제로 맡아서 운영하는 일이에요. 포스터에서 '주최'는 행사를 연 곳, '주관'은 운영을 맡은 곳, '후원'은 돈으로 돕는 곳으로 나뉘어 나와요. '주관적'(subjective)의 '주관'과는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: Means actually taking charge of and running an event. On posters, '주최' is who holds the event, '주관' is who runs it, and '후원' is who supports it with money. It is not the same word as the '주관' in '주관적' (subjective).

examples.en: City Hall carries out this year's budget.
The police enforced the law fairly.

examples.ko: 회사는 다음 달부터 광고비를 집행할 거예요.
examples.en: The company will start spending its ad budget next month.
We record where all the money being spent goes.
After carrying out the plan, we checked the results.

examples.ko: 판결을 그대로 집행한 뒤 사건이 끝났어요.
examples.en: After the ruling was carried out as it was, the case ended.

explain: 정해 둔 계획, 법, 예산을 권한이 있는 곳이 실제로 실행할 때 써요. '실행하다'는 누구나 하는 일에 쓰지만 '집행하다'는 정부, 회사, 법원 같은 공식적인 곳에서 주로 해요. 뉴스와 공문서에는 많이 나오고 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요.
explain_en: Used when an authorized body actually carries out a set plan, law or budget. '실행하다' is for anyone, but '집행하다' mostly belongs to governments, companies and courts. It is common in news and official documents and rare in everyday talk.

examples.en: Student opinions are reflected in the class.
My idea was reflected in the plan.

examples.ko: 새 규칙은 다음 달부터 반영될 거예요.
examples.en: The new rule will take effect from next month.
So much was incorporated that the document got longer.
After the request was taken in, the menu changed.

examples.ko: 화가의 성격이 그림에 반영돼서 그림이 밝아요.
examples.en: The painter's personality shows in the painting, so it is bright.

explain: 의견, 요청, 성격 같은 것이 결과물 안에 들어가서 보일 때 써요. '~에 반영되다'처럼 '에'와 함께 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 사람이 의견을 넣으면 '반영하다', 결과에 들어가 있으면 '반영되다'예요.
explain_en: Used when opinions, requests or personality get included in and show up in a result. It often takes '에': '~에 반영되다'. A person who includes it does '반영하다'; once it is in the result it is '반영되다'.

examples.en: The company takes customer opinions into account.
The teacher incorporated the question into the class.

examples.ko: 우리는 내일 새 의견을 반영할 거예요.
examples.en: We will incorporate the new opinions tomorrow.
It takes time to incorporate opinions.
A painting reflects the look of its era.
I sent the file with the corrections applied.

explain: 의견이나 요청을 실제 결과에 넣는다는 점이 '듣다'와 달라요. '의견을 반영해 주세요'처럼 부탁할 때도 자주 써요. 작품이나 말이 사회와 시대를 그대로 비춰 보여 줄 때도 써서 '시대를 반영하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Unlike '듣다' (listen), it means actually putting opinions or requests into the result, and you can ask '의견을 반영해 주세요'. It is also used when a work or statement mirrors a society or era, as in '시대를 반영하다'.

en: with a light tap; with a pop

examples.en: My friend tapped me lightly on the shoulder.
The soda fizzes sharply in my mouth.
Flick off the dust and have a seat.
A drop of water plopped onto the window.
I nudged the ball lightly and it rolled away.
The berry burst with a pop.

explain: 작고 가벼운 것이 부딪히거나 터지는 소리와 모양을 나타내요. '톡 치다', '톡 털다', '톡 쏘다'처럼 짝이 정해진 동사가 많아요. 비슷한 '탁'은 더 세고 단단한 느낌이라서 '탁 치다'는 훨씬 강해요.
explain_en: Imitates the sound and look of something small and light hitting or popping. It pairs with set verbs such as '톡 치다' (tap), '톡 털다' (flick off) and '톡 쏘다' (sting/fizz). The similar '탁' feels harder and stronger, so '탁 치다' is much firmer.

examples.en: Because of heavy rain, they suspend the construction.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 약을 당분간 중지하라고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me to stop the medicine for a while.
I will pause exercising from tomorrow.
Please explain the reason for stopping first.

examples.ko: 서비스를 중지하고 나서 사과 글을 올렸어요.
examples.en: After suspending the service, they posted an apology.
They halted the match because it was dangerous.

explain: 하던 일을 중간에 멈출 때 써요. '멈추다'는 움직임이나 소리가 서는 일이고, '그만두다'는 아예 끝내는 일이에요. '중지하다'는 공사나 서비스처럼 정해진 일을 멈추고 나중에 다시 할 수 있을 때도 써요.
explain_en: Used when you stop something partway. '멈추다' is for motion or sound coming to a halt, and '그만두다' means quitting for good. '중지하다' fits planned work such as construction or a service that is halted and may resume later.
